quote_original: Recently I read a book called, Vanished Parts of Yesterday, by Lord Frederick Hamilton.
context_after: In it he tells the story of Catherine the Great – who, when she found the first violet of spring, ordered a sentry to be placed over it to protect it from being plucked. Forgetting to rescind the order, day and night, summer and winter, a sentry stood where 150 years ago, a violet bloomed. The new generation did not know why the sentry was there and he didn’t either. It was simply a tradition!
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).
